issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may set aside an acquittal when its review of the evidence and the reasons for acquittal shows that the acquittal was not justified.
material_facts: The trial court found that the deceased party had deadly weapons and relied on that finding to uphold the accused persons’ claim of private defence.
The High Court found that the trial court’s finding about those weapons rested on conjecture and was contrary to the evidence, and explained why it reversed the acquittal.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in interfering with the acquittal because the trial court’s conclusion rested on an unsupported finding and the High Court gave reasons for holding the acquittal unjustified.
issues.legal_principle: An appellate court hearing an appeal against acquittal may review the entire evidence and reach its own conclusion, but must consider the evidence and the reasons supporting the acquittal and state why the acquittal was unjustified. The Court relied on Sheo Swarup v. Emperor, Sanwant Singh v. State of Rajasthan, and Harbans Singh v. State of Punjab.

predicates.appeal_against_acquittal: The proceeding is an appeal seeking reversal of an acquittal.
predicates.trial_finding_based_on_conjecture: The trial court relied on a factual finding that was based on conjecture and contrary to the evidence.
predicates.reviewing_court_explains_why_acquittal_u: The reviewing court considers the evidence and gives reasons why the acquittal was unjustified.

issues.definition: When an acquittal appeal concerns a conjectural trial finding and the reviewing court explains why the acquittal was unjustified, reversal of the acquittal is justified.

issues.legal_issue: Participants acting with a common intention to kill are liable for murder unless the killing is excused by a right of private defence that extends to causing death.
material_facts: The accused were found to be in possession of the field and entitled to cut the crop, but the deceased had a serious claim to possession supported by a civil decree and an order of relinquishment.

The deceased party went to harvest the crop under police protection, after lodging reports expressing apprehension of trouble; the evidence showed peaceful intentions and no dangerous weapons among the deceased party.
The accused attempted to send away the constables, then entered the field armed with guns and a spear and attacked the deceased at close range, killing three people; the accused were not injured.
The evidence established that the accused shared an intention to kill and participated in the attack.
The accused had an opportunity to seek assistance from public authorities but instead diverted a constable on a false pretext and used force that was more than necessary for defence.
issues.conclusion: The accused had no right of private defence extending to causing death, and their common intention and participation made them liable for murder.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code creates joint criminal liability where persons share a common intention and participate in acts in furtherance of it; it does not create a separate offence. Sections 96 and 98 provide that an act done in lawful private defence is not an offence. Under Section 103, private defence of property extends to causing death only for specified offences and subject to Section 99. Section 99 excludes the right where there is time to seek protection from public authorities and limits the right to harm necessary for defence. The Court held that the property-taking shown did not justify causing death, that there was no reasonable apprehension of death or hurt, and that the armed attack was unnecessary and excessive.

rule.if: criminal_homicide_case and shared_intention_to_kill and participation_in_attack and victims_peacefully_harvesting_crop and victims_lacked_dangerous_weapons and attackers_used_deadly_force_without_warning and public_authority_protection_was_available

predicates.criminal_homicide_case: The proceeding concerns a charge arising from a killing.
predicates.shared_intention_to_kill: The participants shared an intention to kill the victims.
predicates.participation_in_attack: Each participant took part in acts advancing the shared intention.
predicates.victims_peacefully_harvesting_crop: The victims were harvesting a crop without attacking the participants.
predicates.victims_lacked_dangerous_weapons: The victims did not possess dangerous weapons for use against the participants.
predicates.attackers_used_deadly_force_without_warn: The participants used deadly force against the victims without warning.
predicates.public_authority_protection_was_availabl: The participants had time and an opportunity to seek protection from public authorities.

issues.definition: In a killing case, participants who share an intention to kill and take part in the attack are liable for murder when the victims are peacefully harvesting without dangerous weapons, the participants use deadly force without warning, and public-authority protection was available.

issues.legal_issue: The exception for culpable homicide committed while exceeding the right of private defence does not apply where the killing is premeditated and the offender intends to cause more harm than necessary for defence.
material_facts: The accused armed themselves and attacked the deceased at close range while the deceased were peacefully harvesting under police protection.
The Court found that the accused acted with a common intention to kill and intended to cause more harm than was necessary for defence.
issues.conclusion: The exception did not apply, and the offence remained murder.
issues.legal_principle: Exception 2 to Section 300 of the Indian Penal Code requires that the offender act in good faith while exercising a right of private defence, exceed the power given by law, cause death without premeditation, and have no intention of doing more harm than necessary for defence. The Court found premeditation and an intention to cause more than necessary harm.

rule.if: criminal_homicide_case and claimed_private_defence and premeditated_killing and intent_to_cause_excessive_harm

predicates.criminal_homicide_case: The proceeding concerns a charge arising from a killing.
predicates.claimed_private_defence: The accused relies on an asserted right to defend a person or property.
predicates.premeditated_killing: The killing was planned or carried out with premeditation.
predicates.intent_to_cause_excessive_harm: The offender intended to cause more harm than was necessary for defence.

issues.definition: When a killing case involves a claim of private defence, premeditation and an intention to cause excessive harm mean that the private-defence exception does not reduce murder.

issues.legal_issue: A person who possesses a firearm without a licence is not exempt from liability merely because the firearm belongs to a close relative who holds a licence.
material_facts: Two accused possessed and used firearms for which they had no licences.
They argued that the firearms belonged to close relatives who held licences.
issues.conclusion: The unlicensed possession attracted liability under Section 19(f) of the Arms Act, and the convictions were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Section 19(f) of the Arms Act applies to possession of a firearm without the required licence; the fact that a licensed close relative owns the firearm does not excuse the possessor.

predicates.criminal_firearm_proceeding: The proceeding includes a charge concerning unlawful firearm possession.
predicates.person_lacked_required_licence: The accused did not hold the required licence for the firearm.

issues.definition: In a firearm-possession proceeding, a person who possessed a firearm without the required licence remains liable for that possession.
